# Scaling and data distribution {#sec-scaling}

::: {.callout-note}
## Stub — planned work
This chapter is not yet run. It is scoped here so the plan is on record.
:::

@sec-data showed the corpus is large but **extremely uneven across children** (per-child pairs
range from 253 to 134,686). Two questions follow, both to be answered in the current design
(all-data training, Gemini gold, Konkle eval) so they are comparable to the ladder of
@sec-bootstrapping. This supersedes the preliminary CLIP-era analysis in @sec-data-whose.

**How much data (scaling).** Subsample the 911k training pairs across a range of sizes and re-run
the ladder, paralleling the count-vs-quality sweep of @sec-experiments. A hypothesis worth stating
up front: the **free** rungs (pure learning, region MIL) should scale with amount — more pairs,
cleaner averages — while the **oracle** rungs (filter, word, vision) are about *information we lack*,
not *amount*, and should stay roughly flat. That contrast would itself be a result: it says the
bottleneck is signal, not scale.

**Whose data (distribution).** Separate *how much* aligned data from *whose*: at matched pair
count, does pooling across many children beat a single child (diversity), and how much does raw
count add on top? The preliminary version (@sec-data-whose) found diversity beats amount at
matched count; the redo tests whether that holds on the clean eval and at the full corpus scale,
and whether within-child models can ever match a pooled model on their own held-out data.
